mainTopic: Greek translation of the תורה, the status of Greek for ספרים, and the 'אין בין' משניות on kinds of כהן גדול, altars, and שילה versus ירושלים
overview: This amud finishes the list of wording changes the זקנים made when they translated the תורה into Greek for King תלמי. Each change avoided a wrong idea about God or an insult to the king. The גמרא then quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says ספרים may be written only in Hebrew or Greek. רבי יוחנן rules like him and learns it from the פסוק 'God shall enlarge יפת.' רבי חייא בר אבא sharpens this reading: only the beauty of יפת, which is Greek, enters the tents of שם. A new משנה compares a כהן גדול anointed with oil to one made by the garments, and a serving כהן גדול to a former one. The גמרא finds that the first line follows the חכמים and the second follows רבי מאיר. רב חסדא and רב יוסף each explain this split in their own way. Next comes a משנה on public and private altars, which the גמרא reads as following רבי שמעון. The amud ends with a משנה comparing שילה to ירושלים, whose last sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משה did not take any valuable thing
steps.stepSummary: The list of changes continues. In the Greek translation, משה's claim 'I did not take one donkey' was written as 'I did not take one valuable thing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote: 'I have not taken one valuable thing from them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a list of places where the זקנים changed the wording when translating the תורה for תלמי. Here they changed משה's words about not taking a donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original פסוק says חמור, a donkey. Read alone, it could sound like משה only avoided taking donkeys but took other things. Writing חמד, any valuable item, makes it clear he took nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A valuable or desirable item
I took / I carried off
King תלמי, who asked for the Greek translation

steps.confusionAlert: The real פסוק says חמור (donkey). The word חמד here is the changed version written for תלמי, not the actual wording of the תורה.

phrases.english: "I have not taken one valuable thing from them."
phrases.notes: The real פסוק says 'one donkey' (חמור). They wrote 'valuable thing' so no one would think משה took other things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of translation changes on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donkey was changed to valuable thing so it is clear משה took nothing at all.

steps.title: The sun and moon were given to give light
steps.stepSummary: In the פסוק about the sun and moon, the זקנים added the word 'to give light,' so it would not sound like God gave them to the nations to worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote: 'Which the Lord your God allotted to give light to all the nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the next change on the list. The זקנים added the word להאיר, 'to give light,' to a פסוק about the heavenly bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the added word, the פסוק could be misread to mean God handed the sun and moon to the nations as objects to worship. The added word explains their real purpose, which is to give light.

keyTerms.meaning: Allotted / gave out as a share
To give light
The nations

phrases.english: "Which the Lord your God allotted them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the sun, moon and stars mentioned in this פסוק.

phrases.english: to give light to all the nations."
phrases.notes: 'To give light' is the added word. It is not in the real פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשֶׁר חָלַק ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֹתָם לְהָאִיר לְכׇל הָעַמִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item on the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'to give light' was added so the פסוק does not sound like it permits the nations to worship the heavenly bodies.

steps.title: Which I did not command them to serve
steps.stepSummary: In the פסוק about serving other gods, the זקנים added 'to serve them,' so it would not sound like God never commanded the sun and moon to exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote: 'And he went and served other gods, which I did not command to serve them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is another change on the list. The זקנים added the word לעובדם, 'to serve them,' at the end of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'which I did not command' could be misread as 'I did not command them to exist,' as if the heavenly bodies made themselves. Adding 'to serve them' shows that God only did not command people to worship them.

keyTerms.meaning: Other gods (idols)
I commanded
To serve them

phrases.english: "And he went and served other gods
which I did not command to serve them."
phrases.notes: 'To serve them' is the added word. Without it, someone could think God never commanded the sun and moon to exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיַּעֲבוֹד אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוִּיתִי לְעוֹבְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item on the same list; it also concerns the heavenly bodies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'To serve them' was added so no one thinks the heavenly bodies came into being without God's command.

steps.title: The hare is called the short-legged animal
steps.stepSummary: The זקנים called the hare 'the short-legged one' instead of ארנבת, because תלמי's wife was named ארנבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote for him 'the short-legged animal,' and did not write 'the hare.' This was because תלמי's wife was named ארנבת. They did not want him to say, 'The Jews mocked me and put my wife's name in the תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last change on the list. Here the reason is not a theological misunderstanding but avoiding an insult to the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארנבת appears in the list of non-kosher animals. If the translation named it, תלמי could think the Jews were mocking his wife, whose name was ארנבת. So they described the animal by a feature, its short legs, instead of by name.

keyTerms.meaning: The short-legged one (literally, 'small of legs')
Hare; also the name of תלמי's wife
They mocked me

steps.whatToRemember: The changes in the Greek translation were made either to prevent a wrong idea about God and the תורה, or to avoid offending the king.

phrases.english: And they wrote for him: "the short-legged animal,"
phrases.notes: 'For him' means for King תלמי, who asked for the translation.

phrases.english: and they did not write for him "the hare,"
because the wife of Ptolemy
was named Arnevet,
so that he would not say: The Jews mocked me
and put my wife's name into the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last item on the list; it gives a political reason instead of a theological one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hare was described rather than named, so the king would not feel mocked.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows only Greek for ספרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: even for ספרים, the only foreign language allowed is Greek.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even for scrolls, they allowed them to be written only in Greek.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the משנה and quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in the משנה allows ספרים to be written in any language. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits this: besides Hebrew, only Greek is allowed. The story of the Greek translation for תלמי helps explain why Greek has this special status.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls of Scripture
Greek
They (the חכמים) permitted

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even for scrolls, they did not permit
that they be written except in Greek.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אַף בַּסְּפָרִים לֹא הִתִּירוּ שֶׁיִּכָּתְבוּ אֶלָּא יְוָנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the story of the translation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספרים may be written in a foreign language only if it is Greek.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final practical ruling on the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן decides the argument. In practice, ספרים may be written in Hebrew or Greek, but not in other foreign languages.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows...

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling turns רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion into the practical law about writing ספרים in Greek.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the opinion just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Greek is the only foreign language allowed for ספרים.

steps.title: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks what the source is for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's special allowance for Greek.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן sets up the next move. He asks why Greek, out of all foreign languages, gets special status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he now explains where the opinion comes from. The question is: what makes Greek different from every other language?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion that was just ruled as הלכה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for giving Greek special status

steps.title: The words of יפת in the tents of שם
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'God shall enlarge יפת, and he shall dwell in the tents of שם.' This means the words of יפת will be in the tents of שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'God shall enlarge יפת, and he shall dwell in the tents of שם.' This means the words of יפת will be in the tents of שם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers his own question with a פסוק from נח's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as saying that the words, meaning the language, of יפת will be in the tents of שם, the place of תורה. Greek counts as יפת's language, because יון was a son of יפת. The next step challenges this reading, and Step 10 refines it to mean the beauty of יפת.

keyTerms.meaning: God shall enlarge (or beautify) יפת
The tents of שם, where תורה is learned

steps.whatToRemember: Greek is special because it is the language of יפת, and the פסוק says the words of יפת may be in the tents of שם.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"God shall enlarge Japheth,
phrases.notes: This is from נח's blessing to his sons. Greece (יון) was one of יפת's sons.

phrases.english: and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל יֶפֶת יִהְיוּ בְּאׇהֳלֵי שֵׁם.
phrases.english: meaning: the words of Japheth shall be in the tents of Shem.
phrases.notes: 'Words of יפת' means his language, Greek, which may be used even for holy ספרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּן בְּאׇהֳלֵי שֵׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about יפת dwelling in the tents of שם shows that Greek may be used inside the holy world of תורה.

steps.title: Why not the languages of גומר and מגוג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from the פסוק: גומר and מגוג were also sons of יפת, so why not allow their languages?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the פסוק means the languages of גומר and מגוג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 8. If the פסוק only says 'the words of יפת,' any language from יפת's family should count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק as read in Step 8 only points to יפת's family in general. גומר and מגוג are also children of יפת, just like יון (Greece). So the proof does not yet explain why Greek alone is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead / maybe it means
Two sons of יפת, brothers of יון (Greece)

phrases.english: But say it means Gomer and Magog?
phrases.notes: גומר and מגוג are listed as sons of יפת in the תורה, right next to יון, who is Greece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק given in Step 8 as too broad.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that 'the words of יפת will be in the tents of שם' singles out Greek.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names יפת in general, so every son of יפת, such as Gomer and Magog, should qualify equally.

steps.title: The beauty of יפת means Greek
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reads יַפְתְּ as 'beauty': only the beauty of יפת, the Greek language, enters the tents of שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: This is the reason, as it is written: 'God shall enlarge יפת.' It means the beauty of יפת shall be in the tents of שם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the challenge by reading the word יַפְתְּ as coming from יוֹפִי, beauty. Only the most beautiful language of יפת's family, Greek, is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק is read more narrowly. It is no longer 'any words of יפת' but 'the beauty of יפת.' This removes גומר and מגוג and leaves only Greek.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
Shall enlarge; here read as related to beauty
His beauty
The tents of שם (the Jewish people)

steps.whatToRemember: Greek is allowed for ספרים because the פסוק speaks of the 'beauty of יפת' entering the tents of שם, and Greek is that beauty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
This is the reason, as it is written:
"God shall enlarge Yefet,"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, but now the word יַפְתְּ is read as sounding like יוֹפִי, beauty.

phrases.english: the beauty of Yefet
shall be in the tents of Shem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9 by narrowing the reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק includes every language of יפת's descendants, like Gomer and Magog.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק refers to the beauty of יפת, which is Greek alone.

steps.title: Anointed כהן גדול versus one made by the extra garments
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the only difference between a כהן גדול anointed with oil and one made by wearing the extra garments is the special bull brought for any of the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There is no difference between a כהן anointed with the anointing oil and one with the extra garments, except the bull brought for any of the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the 'אין בין' pattern of listing the only difference between two similar things. It compares two kinds of כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are true כהנים גדולים; one became so through שמן המשחה, the other through wearing the eight garments. The only difference is that only the anointed one brings the special פר when he rules in error and acts on it in a sin requiring a קרבן חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
There is no difference between
A כהן גדול anointed with oil
A כהן גדול made by wearing the extra garments
The bull brought for an accidental sin in any of the מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: Both are fully כהנים גדולים. The משנה is not saying the one with extra garments is a lesser category, only that he does not bring this one קרבן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is no difference between a priest anointed
with the anointing oil
and one with the extra garments
phrases.notes: This is a כהן גדול who was put into office by wearing the special clothes, without the oil.

phrases.english: except the bull that is brought
for any of the מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִמְרוּבֵּה בְגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, continuing the chapter's 'אין בין' list with a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An anointed כהן גדול and one made by the garments differ only in the פר הבא על כל המצות.

steps.title: Serving כהן גדול versus former כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's second line: the only difference between the current כהן גדול and a former one is the יום הכפורים bull and the daily tenth of an איפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difference between a serving כהן and a former כהן, except the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of the איפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second comparison: a כהן גדול now serving versus one who filled in and then stepped down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The former כהן גדול keeps the status of a כהן גדול in most ways. Only two קרבנות belong to the one serving now: the bull of יום הכפורים and the daily flour offering of a tenth of an איפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול currently serving
A former כהן גדול who has stepped down
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
The daily flour offering of a tenth of an איפה

phrases.english: There is no difference between a serving priest
and a former priest
phrases.notes: He means someone who filled in as כהן גדול and stepped down when the original returned; he keeps the sanctity of a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: except the bull of Yom Kippur
and the tenth of the ephah.
phrases.notes: This is the flour offering the כהן גדול brings every day, half in the morning and half in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second clause of the same משנה, adding a parallel comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A serving כהן גדול and a former one differ only in the פר יום הכפורים and the עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: Inference: both kinds of כהן גדול bring the יום הכפורים bull and daily offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the first line of the משנה that the anointed כהן גדול and the one made by garments are the same regarding the יום הכפורים bull and the tenth of the איפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that regarding the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of the איפה, this one and that one are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the משנה's wording and draws a conclusion. It is setting up a discussion of this inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה listed only one difference (the פר הבא על כל המצות) between the anointed and the garment-made כהן גדול, everything else must be the same. That means both bring the יום הכפורים bull and the עשירית האיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion on the משנה
This implies
This one and that one are equal

steps.confusionAlert: 'This and that' here means the anointed כהן גדול and the garment-made כהן גדול from the first line, not the serving and former כהן from the second line.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that regarding the bull of Yom Kippur
and the tenth of the ephah,
this one and that one are equal.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול anointed with oil and the one who got the job by wearing the garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן פַּר יוֹם כִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the first line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication of the משנה, the anointed and the garment-made כהן גדול are equal regarding the פר יום הכפורים and the עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the first line of the משנה goes against רבי מאיר. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי מאיר says a כהן גדול made by the garments also brings the special bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי מאיר. If it were, there is a problem, because a ברייתא teaches: a כהן גדול made by wearing the extra garments does bring the bull for any of the מצוות. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say he does not bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose opinion the first line of the משנה follows. It shows that רבי מאיר cannot be the author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the only difference between the two kinds of כהן גדול is the bull for the מצוות, so the one made by garments does not bring it. רבי מאיר says he does bring it. So the משנה must follow the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול made by wearing the extra high-priest garments, without the anointing oil
The bull a כהן גדול brings when he sins by mistake, through a wrong ruling, on any of the מצוות
But a ברייתא teaches, which introduces a source that causes a problem

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir,
for if it were Rabbi Meir, [isn't it taught]:
one consecrated by multiple garments brings a bull
that is brought for any of the מצוות,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir,
and the Rabbis say: he does not bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading of the first line of the משנה from steps 11 and 13 to identify which תנא wrote it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first line of the משנה follows the חכמים, not רבי מאיר, who holds that the מרובה בגדים also brings the bull for the מצוות.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר learns that a כהן גדול made by garments brings the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי מאיר's view. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a 'משיח', an anointed priest, so it is surprising that רבי מאיר includes a כהן גדול who was never anointed. The גמרא wants to see how he reads the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason, a request for the source

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבי מאיר view quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק-based source showing that a מרובה בגדים brings the bull for the מצוות.

steps.title: The extra letter ה in 'הַמָּשִׁיחַ' includes the garment-made כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the word 'הַמָּשִׁיחַ' with its extra ה as including a כהן גדול made by the garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: from 'משיח' alone, I would only know about one anointed with the anointing oil. From where do we know a כהן גדול made by the extra garments? The פסוק says 'הַמָּשִׁיחַ', THE anointed one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that finds רבי מאיר's source in the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'משיח' would mean only the oil-anointed כהן גדול. The added ה, 'the', widens it to any כהן גדול, including one made by wearing the garments. So he too brings the bull.

keyTerms.meaning: The special anointing oil used to anoint a כהן גדול
The פסוק teaches, which introduces the word that gives the answer
THE anointed one; the extra ה adds to the meaning

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Anointed";
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק about a כהן גדול who sins, in ויקרא chapter 4.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה,
phrases.english: I have only one anointed with the oil of anointing;
from where do we know one consecrated by multiple garments?
The verse states: "The anointed."
phrases.notes: The extra ה, meaning 'the', is what includes the garment-made כהן גדול.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מָשִׁיחַ, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns from the extra ה in 'הַמָּשִׁיחַ' that a מרובה בגדים is treated like an anointed כהן גדול for the bull.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole מחלוקת depends on how much weight the extra ה carries.

steps.title: The second line of the משנה seems to follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem: the first line is not רבי מאיר, but the second line, which says a former כהן גדול is equal to a current one in everything else, matches רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did we explain the משנה? As not following רבי מאיר. Now say the next line: the only difference between a serving כהן גדול and a former one is the יום הכפורים bull and the tenth of an איפה. That means in everything else, they are the same. That brings us to רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion of step 14 by showing that the next line of the same משנה points to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single משנה should not switch authors mid-way. The first line shows the author is not רבי מאיר. But the second line keeps the former כהן גדול fully a כהן גדול in all other things, and that is רבי מאיר's view, as the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: How did we establish it? It recalls an earlier conclusion in order to challenge it
Say the latter part, meaning look at the next line of the משנה
A former כהן גדול who no longer serves
We have arrived at, meaning this matches someone's opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lines. The first line compares oil-anointed vs garment-made. The second compares current vs former. Each line points to a different תנא.

phrases.english: How did we establish it?
As not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.
Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר
phrases.english: The difference between a serving priest and a former priest is

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה.
phrases.english: only the Yom Kippur bull and the tenth of an ephah.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין,
phrases.english: This implies that in all other matters, this one and that one are equal;
we have arrived at Rabbi Meir,

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְנָא — דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר. אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 14 conclusion by using the second line of the משנה from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second line implies a former כהן גדול keeps all high-priest status except two items, and that is רבי מאיר's view. So the first and second lines would follow different תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי מאיר's view on a replacement כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that רבי מאיר keeps a replaced כהן גדול under all the high-priest rules, while רבי יוסי says he is fit neither as כהן גדול nor as a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: if the כהן גדול became temporarily unfit and they appointed another כהן in his place, the first goes back to his service. The second still has all the מצוות of a כהן גדול on him. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יוסי says: the first goes back to his service, and the second is fit neither as כהן גדול nor as a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the second line of the משנה matches רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the replacement who stepped down is still bound by all high-priest rules. That fits the משנה's 'in everything else they are equal'. רבי יוסי disagrees and leaves him unable to serve at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Something happened that made him unfit to serve for a while
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
Goes back to his service as כהן גדול

phrases.english: as it is taught: If disqualification befell him,
and they appointed another priest in his stead,
the first returns to his service;

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי — כׇּל מִצְוֹת כְּהוּנָּה גְּדוֹלָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: the second, all the מצוות of the High Priesthood are upon him;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: רִאשׁוֹן — חוֹזֵר לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: The first returns to his service;

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי — אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לֹא לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: the second is fit neither as High Priest
nor as a common priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵירַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל וּמִינּוּ כֹּהֵן אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind 'אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר' in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That the second line of the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי מאיר keeps all high-priest מצוות on the replacement כהן, against רבי יוסי

steps.title: רבי יוסי's story of רבי יוסף בן אלם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי supports his view with a real case. רבי יוסף בן אלם replaced a כהן גדול who became unfit, and the חכמים ruled that the replacement is fit for neither role.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: there was a case with רבי יוסף בן אלם from ציפורי. The כהן גדול became unfit, and they appointed him in his place. The case came before the חכמים, and they said: the first goes back to his service, and the second is fit neither as כהן גדול nor as a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his position with an actual event where the חכמים ruled like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds practical support to רבי יוסי's side of the מחלוקת. The גמרא first explains the reasoning of this ruling (step 20). It then states the problem fully (step 21) and answers it in steps 22 and 23.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual event, brought as support for a ruling
ציפורי, a city in the Galilee
They appointed him in his place

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף בֶּן אִלֵּם מִצִּיפּוֹרִי
phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabbi Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori,
where disqualification befell the High Priest,
and they appointed him in his stead,
and the incident came before the Sages,
and they said: The first returns to his service;

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי — אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לֹא לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל וְלֹא לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: the second is fit neither as High Priest nor as a common priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף בֶּן אִלֵּם מִצִּיפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by giving רבי יוסי's supporting story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's ruling that the replacement כהן גדול is fit for neither role
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רבי יוסף בן אלם, decided by the חכמים
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's first line follows the חכמים against רבי מאיר, but its second line matches רבי מאיר against רבי יוסי. Steps 22 and 23 explain this mix.

steps.title: Why the replacement fits neither role
steps.stepSummary: The reason he cannot be כהן גדול is the jealousy it would cause. The reason he cannot be a כהן הדיוט is that we raise in holiness and do not lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: He cannot serve as a כהן גדול because of hatred. He cannot serve as a regular כהן because we go up in holiness and never down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the case of רבי יוסף בן אלם from Step 19. It gives the reason the חכמים said the replacement is fit for neither role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate reasons block the two roles. Keeping him as a second כהן גדול would create jealousy and bad feeling with the original one. Sending him back down to a regular כהן would break the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.

keyTerms.meaning: Hatred or bad feeling, here the jealousy between two כהנים גדולים
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
We raise people in holiness and do not lower them

steps.whyThisMatters: מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין is a principle that shows up in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: Not as a High Priest, because of hatred;
not as a common priest,
because we raise in holiness and do not lower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the ruling of the חכמים in the story from Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A replacement כהן גדול cannot keep the high role because of jealousy, and cannot go back down because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.

steps.title: The משנה seems to follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The first line of the משנה follows the רבנן and the second line follows רבי מאיר. Can one משנה really switch like that?
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first line follows the רבנן and the last line follows רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem that has been building since Step 17. Our משנה appears to follow one opinion in its first half and a different opinion in its second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line leaves out the כהן גדול made only by the garments. That does not match רבי מאיר, who includes him (Step 16). The second line treats a former כהן גדול like a current one, and that is רבי מאיר's view (Step 18). A single משנה should not normally switch authors in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The Sages, the majority opinion against a single named תנא

phrases.english: The first clause is the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: This is the line about the כהן גדול made by the garments, who is left out of the bull. That is not רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir?!
phrases.notes: This is the line saying a former כהן גדול is equal to a current one, which matches Step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא opened in Step 17. The first line matches the חכמים who argue with רבי מאיר about the bull (Step 14). The second line matches רבי מאיר against רבי יוסי about a former כהן גדול (Step 18). So the משנה seems split.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה's authorship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first line does not fit רבי מאיר, and the second line fits only רבי מאיר, so the משנה seems to have two authors.

steps.title: רב חסדא accepts the split
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says yes, the first line really is the רבנן and the second line really is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Yes. The first line is the רבנן and the last line is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by simply agreeing that the משנה is split between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not try to make the משנה fit one תנא. He accepts that a משנה can have two lines that come from two different authors.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: Indeed,
the first clause is the Rabbis,
and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the premise: the משנה really has two authors
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה should follow one author all the way through.
steps.terutzMaskana: This משנה is split: the רבנן in the first line and רבי מאיר in the second.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is all רבי, choosing between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the whole משנה is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who sided with a different תנא on each issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי, and he arranged it following different תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second answer. One author wrote the whole משנה, but he holds like different תנאים on different points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה has one author after all. רבי holds like the רבנן about the כהן גדול made by the garments and like רבי מאיר about a former כהן גדול. That makes his position a third view, built from both.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranges it following different תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying the משנה has two authors. He is saying one author agrees with the רבנן on one point and with רבי מאיר on another.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the split משנה. רב חסדא says two different authors wrote it. רב יוסף says רבי wrote it all and mixed opinions on purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi,
phrases.notes: This means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: and he takes it according to different tanna'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same קשיא that רב חסדא answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Single author who agrees with different תנאים on different issues
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A split between רבנן and רבי מאיר means two authors.
steps.terutzMaskana: One author, רבי, holds a combined view of his own.

steps.title: New משנה: public altar versus private altar
steps.stepSummary: The only difference between a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה and a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is פסחים. The rule is that voluntary offerings may go on a בָּמָה and required offerings may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only difference between a big public altar and a small private altar is פסחים. The rule: anything that can be vowed or donated is offered on a private בָּמָה, and anything that is neither vowed nor donated is not offered on a private בָּמָה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the משנה's list of 'the only difference between X and Y.' This one compares the public altar with a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the times when private altars were allowed, a person could bring offerings on his own בָּמָה. The משנה says a קרבן פסח could not be brought there. It then gives a wider rule: only voluntary offerings could be brought on a private altar, and required offerings could not.

keyTerms.meaning: The big public altar, like the ones at נוב and גבעון
A small private altar built by an individual
Brought because of a vow (נדר) or as a freewill gift (נדבה)
This is the general rule

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is no difference between a great altar
and a small altar except Paschal lambs.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא נִידָּר וְנִידָּב —
phrases.english: This is the principle: anything that is vowed or donated
is offered on a small altar,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא נִידָּר וְלֹא נִידָּב —
phrases.english: and anything that is neither vowed nor donated
is not offered on a small altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה לַבָּמָה קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא פְּסָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה in the same 'אין בין' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only voluntary offerings may be brought on a private בָּמָה. פסחים and other required offerings may not.

steps.title: Is פסחים really the only difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the only difference is פסחים, since the משנה's own rule seems to exclude more offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only פסחים and nothing else?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה contradicts itself. It says 'only פסחים,' but its general rule leaves out every required offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זה הכלל says that anything not vowed or donated cannot go on a private altar. That covers many required offerings, not only the פסח. So the word 'only' in the first line seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Paschal lambs and nothing more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'only פסחים' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's own general rule leaves out all required offerings, so פסחים cannot be the only difference.

steps.title: Read it as 'offerings like פסחים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says to read the משנה as 'offerings similar to פסחים.' That means the whole group of required offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: offerings like פסחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה. 'פסחים' stands for a whole group of offerings, not just the פסח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כעין פסחים' means offerings that are like the פסח: required offerings that come at a fixed time and are not vowed or donated. Now the first line agrees with the זה הכלל, and nothing contradicts. Step 28 explains why only fixed-time required offerings make the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it as
Similar to, like

steps.whatToRemember: פסחים in this משנה stands for every offering like it, meaning all required offerings. Those cannot be brought on a private בָּמָה.

phrases.english: Say: similar to Paschal lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא by rereading the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פסחים' means every offering similar to the פסח, meaning required offerings with a fixed time. These go on the big בָּמָה but not on a small one (as Step 28 shows from רבי שמעון).

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view in the משנה as just explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the rule it just explained. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 read the משנה as 'offerings like פסחים,' meaning required offerings. Now the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that view, so the rule has a known source.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Which תנא holds this view?

phrases.english: Who is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the rule as it was read in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that only required offerings like פסחים are left off the small בָּמָה, while the big בָּמָה takes them?

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, proven from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The view belongs to רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows he holds that even the public brought only פסחים and fixed-time required offerings, and that required offerings with no fixed time were brought on no בָּמָה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: Even the public brought only פסחים and required offerings that have a fixed time. But required offerings with no fixed time were not brought here or there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון. It quotes a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says that even on the big public בָּמָה, the only required offerings were פסחים and others with a set time, like the fixed public offerings. Required offerings with no set time, like a קרבן brought for a mistake, were not brought on either kind of בָּמָה. That explains why the משנה says 'like פסחים': it means only required offerings with a fixed time.

keyTerms.meaning: The public, the whole community
Required offerings
Has a fixed, set time
Here and here, meaning both kinds of בָּמָה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the big בָּמָה took only required offerings with a fixed time, like פסחים. Required offerings with no fixed time waited for the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon.
As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even the public did not bring
anything except Paschal offerings and required offerings
that have a fixed time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶם זְמַן —
phrases.english: but required offerings that have no fixed time —
were not brought here or there.
phrases.notes: Not on the small בָּמָה and not on the big one either. They had to wait for the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27 and backs it up with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון. For him, only fixed-time required offerings like פסחים were brought on the big בָּמָה, and required offerings with no fixed time were brought on no בָּמָה.

steps.title: New משנה: where lighter offerings are eaten in שילה versus ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The only difference between שילה and ירושלים is the area for eating קדשים קלים and מעשר שני. In שילה it is anywhere you can see the town from. In ירושלים it is only inside the city walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only difference between שילה and ירושלים is this: in שילה you eat קדשים קלים and מעשר שני anywhere you can see שילה from, and in ירושלים only inside the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares the משכן at שילה with the בית המקדש in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier lines in this פרק, this one uses the pattern 'the only difference between X and Y.' In שילה, lighter offerings and מעשר שני could be eaten in any spot from which שילה could be seen. In ירושלים the limit was the city wall.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש
Offerings of lighter holiness, like a שלמים
The second tithe, eaten in the holy place
Any place from which you can see (שילה)
The city wall

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is no difference between Shiloh and Jerusalem,
except that in Shiloh one eats
offerings of lesser holiness and the second tithe
in any place that sees it,
and in Jerusalem, only inside the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the בָּמָה discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שילה, קדשים קלים and מעשר שני are eaten anywhere שילה can be seen from. In ירושלים they are eaten only inside the walls.

steps.title: What both places share: the holiest offerings stay inside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: In both שילה and ירושלים, קדשי קדשים are eaten only inside the courtyard, behind the hangings.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both places, the holiest offerings are eaten only inside the hangings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a rule that is the same in both places. The holiest offerings must be eaten inside the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not another difference. It shows that the gap between שילה and ירושלים was only for the lighter offerings. For קדשי קדשים, both places used the courtyard as the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness, like a חטאת or אשם
The cloth hangings that formed the courtyard fence
Both here and there, in both places

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this line as a second difference between the two places. 'וכאן וכאן' means the rule is the same in both.

phrases.english: And both here and there,
offerings of the highest holiness are eaten
only inside the hangings.
phrases.notes: Inside the courtyard. The courtyard of the משכן was fenced with cloth hangings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule that is the same in both places, after the one difference given in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both שילה and ירושלים, קדשי קדשים are eaten only inside the courtyard.

steps.title: Opening the next point: the holiness of שילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new point about how the holiness of שילה worked. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The holiness of שילה...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next point, about the holiness of שילה. The rest of the sentence comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה turns to a new topic: what kind of holiness שילה had. We only see the opening words here, so wait for the next passage to learn the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of שילה

phrases.english: The sanctity of Shiloh —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a statement about the holiness of שילה. The ruling itself comes on the next amud.
